What is Swing Trading?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

DETAILED DEFINITION

Swing trading describes a holding-period style in which positions commonly remain open across multiple sessions. It is not a standardized contract or proof that a particular schedule suits someone with a job or school commitments. Prices can gap during closed sessions, and an intended exit can execute at a different price or fail during a halt or outage. Chart intervals and review schedules are choices rather than universal professional standards. Compare holding windows using matching dates, costs and assumptions, keeping missed reviews and adverse cases in the record. TradeHQ’s instant practice fills omit real order-book execution.

HOW IT WORKS

Holding positions across sessions, commonly for days or weeks. Review schedules and chart intervals vary; gaps and execution risks remain.

KEY POINTS
Holds positions days to weeks to capture medium-term moves
Chart intervals are choices for the stated exercise rather than a universal requirement
Time requirements vary with the process and instruments; no universal daily schedule is established
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Compare a multi-day holding window with a shorter one, including gaps between observations. No holding period is a universal best starting method for beginners.

Worked exercise and its limits

A hypothetical share bought at $50 with an intended manual exit at $48 opens at $45 next session. For 20 shares, loss at $45 is $100 before costs, not the intended $40. Holding across sessions leaves gap and execution exposure.

References and scope
SEC Investor.gov — market, limit and stop order mechanics
